note:
v1, WHOLE (first round, composed from scratch): MARGINALLY BOUND, the innermost orbit and the album's crest. 132 -> 150 bpm (flat across both 16-bar seams), 176 bars, 301 s; render RTF ~0.31 on 2 threads.
- E7 "the jet" (posted in motifs.md): the Lydian collection as one column of fifths fired upward and accelerating, D3 A3 E4 B4 F#5 C#6 G#6 on 2 2 2 1 1 1 2 sixteenths (11, prime).
- THE STORM A SEMITONE ABOVE HOME: t7 takes t6's unresolved Eb; every element transformed there: E1 in a three-speed stretto (vosim bell x1, Game Boy wave squeezed x2, modal bell stretched x2), E2's seven on the rimshot/snare ghosts, E3 squeezed x2 on a reese (two saws + sine, no resonance), E4 at half harmonic rhythm in its storm minor (cz-pad stabs), E5 squeezed into a trill, E6's tide squeezed to a one-beat Eb|D pull; a bytebeat under the collision; the jet tries to fire in fragments; dusty-kit break with stutter/crush lanes.
- Every cycle (20/10/40, 7, 14, 40, 6, 11 sixteenths) is phased to land on bar 120, where Eb resolves to D and the album crests: the jet fires whole every cycle (doubled on an NES pulse), E6 resolves to D only, E3 re-barred to the bar, and a choir (tts --sing --mode choir) sings "each lap a little shorter" (in Eb fragments in the collision, whole in the slack and the crest). A SLACK (bars 81-88: the tide frozen on Eb, the choir alone), a riser, a master tapestop at the plunge.
- Seams: in, takes t6's Eb (E6 frozen, an Eb1 floor under the cello blur; flow in 3.3 dB / 3.0); out, the jet stops, E1 stretched x4 stops on its E4 and holds it over an open D-A-E (no third) for t8's E8 (out 0.3 dB / 7.3).
- Scores: s0 97.918 / s11 97.929 (spectrum 89.1: still 114 Hz short; flow 81). -11.1 LUFS, TP -1.29.
